page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY cores running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for boot and data volumes.

The underlying x86_64 architecture supports several advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX and AVX512F), AES cryptography, and bit manipulation instructions like BMI2, ADX, and FMA. However, it lacks support for newer deep learning and matrix acceleration extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI, AVX VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and AMX.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.n2.medium in the lower tiers relative to modern cloud hardware. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1107.09 is categorized as weak, while the multi-core score of 2193.58 is poor. Memory bandwidth tests show a similar trend, with uncached read-only large block bandwidth at 16.61 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 14.38 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations also register in the bottom 10%, indicating significant performance limitations for high-throughput workloads.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation but lower-tier benchmark results, the ecs.n2.medium offers an entry-level hardware profile. It is suitable for low-intensity workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but do not demand high computational or memory throughput. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, lightweight application hosting, development environments, and simple background tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio but lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmark data indicates modest performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU scores falling into the bottom 25% and 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read speeds of 16.61 GB/sec. Consequently, the ecs.n2.medium is best suited for low-intensity workloads such as basic web serving, development environments, and lightweight background processing where dedicated CPU allocation is required but high computational throughput is not critical.
